claims.text: Alcohol consumption increases high density lipoprotein cholesterol levels.
Alcohol consumption increases apolipoprotein A1 levels.
Alcohol consumption shows a dose-response relation with high density lipoprotein cholesterol levels.
Alcohol consumption does not affect triglyceride levels.

evidence.description: Pooled mean difference for high density lipoprotein cholesterol was 0.094 mmol/L (95% CI 0.064 to 0.123).
Pooled mean difference for apolipoprotein A1 was 0.101 g/L (95% CI 0.073 to 0.129).
Pooled mean difference for adiponectin was 0.56 mg/L (95% CI 0.39 to 0.72).
Test for trend P = 0.013 for high density lipoprotein cholesterol.
Fibrinogen levels decreased by -0.20 g/L (95% CI -0.29 to -0.11).
Alcohol did not affect triglyceride levels in meta-analysis.

methodologies.name: Systematic review and meta-analysis of interventional studies
methodologies.description: Systematic search of Medline and Embase to review and meta-analyse fixed or random effects models evaluating the effects of alcohol consumption on biological markers of coronary heart disease.
conditions: Comparison of fasting levels of biological markers after alcohol use vs after a period of no alcohol use (controls)
Stratification by beverage type (wine, beer, spirits)
Sensitivity analysis grouped by study design
